clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory quest that instructs adventurers in the art of fashioning wilderness furnishings from harvested animal pelts. It directs skilled skinners to Balthus Stoneflayer in Ironforge to learn how to craft a comfortable Camp Chair for their campsite.

Skinning fallen beasts is among the most practical disciplines an adventurer can cultivate while traversing the wilds of Azeroth. Beyond supplying raw leather for armorers and crafters, the hides gathered from predatory cats, bears, and beasts can be repurposed directly in the field. This introductory task directs skinners to transform raw materials into practical wilderness amenities rather than simply selling them off.

The quest sends skinning practitioners to seek out Balthus Stoneflayer in the dwarven capital of Ironforge. Balthus knows the secrets of turning prepared animal pelts into a functional Camp Chair. However, he demands that an adventurer first demonstrate clear proficiency in the art of skinning before he agrees to impart his crafting techniques.

Life on the road takes a heavy physical toll on travelers and hunters alike. A sturdy Camp Chair offers an adventurer a chance to sit down and unwind by the fire, regaining their energy and sharp senses. Taking a moment to recuperate ensures that when the next dangerous dust-up begins, the adventurer is fighting at peak condition and can strike where it counts.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Being able to skillfully harvest the skins and hides of fallen beasts is one of the more valuable skills an adventurer can possess.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Camp Chair for your camp. Sometimes it's important to just take a load off, and you can use some of those hides you've gathered to make a comfy chair to sit in. A bit of relaxation can help ensure that you are at your peak condition and can strike where it counts the next time you find yourself in a dust-up.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own Camp Chair. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
